conviction_note: Lean is mildly negative on Q3 revenue (company said its August trend supported the low end of the guide while consensus sits at the midpoint, compares tighten about 4 points, UBS saw website traffic slow, October clothing-store sales fell), partly offset by a probable EPS-guide raise from Section 301 tariff relief the company quantified at $35M but left out of the guide. That relief is the pattern that bought +12.9% in August. The stock is down 16.9% in 20 days, so expectations have already reset. p_up 48 on 12.5 points of absolute move gives -0.5. The findings sum to -0.7 and the two numbers agree in sign and size.
bar: Revenue $4.02B, from two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/GAP/23177, 2026-11-11) and Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/gap-earnings-on-deck-can-gap-brand-offset-old-navy-woes-93CH-5039321, 2026-11-19). That is the midpoint of the company's Q3 guide of +1.5% to +2.5% on a $3.94B base, about $4.00-4.04B (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000039911/000162828026059262/q22026eprexhibit991.htm). Q3 EPS consensus is DISPUTED: $0.73 at Earnings Whispers, whisper $0.75; $0.76 in the sweep row; $0.78 at Investing.com. No finding is sized on EPS. Full-year adjusted EPS guide is $2.35-2.45 against a $2.33 consensus (Earnings Whispers).
positioning_check: Short interest 23,806,271 shares at the 2026-10-30 FINRA settlement, 4.87 days to cover, about 6.8% of shares outstanding, trending down from 30.2M in July (https://equibles.com/stocks/gap/shortinterest). UBS put it at 9.7% of float on 2026-11-10 and called buyer positioning crowded at 12.9 against a 2.6 historical and 4.2 sector average (https://www.tradingsat.com/actualites/informations-societes/gap-flechit-a-wall-street-ubs-prevoit-des-resultats-sans-relief-1173538.html). Since that note the stock went from about $21.8 to $19.045, so part of that long has probably unwound. Not a crowded short. 25-delta skew is +1.02 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.17, straddle-implied move 11.26% against a median historical reaction of 14.41%. Run-up is -10.38% over 5 days and -16.87% over 20 days, 3.8% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: At the Q2 call on 2026-08-27 the CFO said of the Q3 guide of +1.5% to +2.5% (about $4.00-4.04B) that 'our current trend supports the low end of our outlook', meaning about $4.00B. Consensus is $4.02B, the midpoint. The Q3 compare is about 4 points tougher than Q2's: Q3 FY25 comps were total +5%, Old Navy +6%, Gap +7%, against Q2 FY25's +1%, +2%, +4%. So Old Navy's flat to down 1% Q3 guide implies a two-year stack of +5 to +6 against -2 in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue and Old Navy have driven this name. Q1 FY26 (2026-05-28): sales miss and full-year sales cut, -15.4%. Q4 FY25 (2026-03-05): disappointing revenue forecast, -14.4%. Q2 FY26 (2026-08-27): sales down 2% and Old Navy -4%, but an EPS beat and raise bought +12.9%. So a modest sales miss with good margins has been forgiven.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $4.02B sits at the guide midpoint rather than the low end the company pointed to, so the sell side has not taken the 'low end' remark into its number. If it had, the revenue consensus would read $4.00B. The miss is inside the company's own guided range, which caps it.
findings.independence: Q3 FY25 brand comps from a separate document (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/gap-stock-eyes-return-to-the-green-this-year-as-viral-denim-campaign-delivers-sydney-sweeney-style-lift-for-q3/cLPMaHQREaM) and Q2 FY25 comps (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39911/000003991125000110/q22025eprexhibit991.htm). The trend remark and the guide come from the same company documents, so they count as one finding.

findings.finding: In a 2026-11-10 preview, UBS (Buy, $42 target) said its internal data show a marked quarter-on-quarter slowdown in website traffic at all four brands: Old Navy, Gap, Banana Republic and Athleta. It expects an in-line Q3, no lift to EPS estimates or the multiple, and an unchanged full-year guide, and warned that crowded long positioning could take profits on that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Old Navy traffic slowing was the stated cause of the Q2 sales miss ('traffic slowing as the quarter progressed'). That print still rose +12.9% on margin and the guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the note was public on 2026-11-10 and the stock has fallen about 12.6% since, from about $21.8 to $19.045. Consensus revenue has not moved off $4.02B, though (Investing.com 2026-11-19 says revenue estimates are flat over 60 days). If the traffic data were in the number, the revenue estimate would have come down.
findings.independence: A broker's proprietary web data, not company numbers. It points the same way as the company's own 'low end' remark (call script, a different source) and the October Census clothing decline (https://www.wcax.com/2026/11/17/spending-growth-slowed-retail-stores-october-high-prices-give-shoppers-pause/).

findings.finding: The Census October 2026 advance retail sales (released 2026-11-17) showed clothing-store sales falling, about -0.7% m/m and the biggest drop since January per secondary reports, while the total rose 0.2%. TJX's Q3 release on 2026-11-18 said 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada' held back demand in some categories. Marmaxx comped +2% on +6%, although TJX's consolidated +4% beat its plan. October is the last month of Gap's Q3 (ended about 2026-10-31), and the warmth carries into the start of the holiday quarter the Q4 guide rests on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Old Navy's fall assortment (denim, sweaters, knits, fleece) is the category weather hits, and seasonal-category misses drove the -15.4% on 2026-05-28.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro proxy that came out two days before the print. Apparel fell on 2026-11-16 (GAP -6.2%) as investors rotated into defensives, so some of it is in the tape. Gap has not commented on October or the weather.
findings.independence: TJX Q3 FY27 release, a direct apparel-retail counterparty that reported after Gap last spoke: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm (2026-11-18). This is a proxy; the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call Gap said: 'If the current rate of 10% holds through the end of the third quarter, we estimate it would provide an additional $35 million of benefit to the year', on top of the $15M already in the raised guide. The Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (10% or 12.5% tiers) took effect 2026-07-24, and no rate change through Q3-end (about 2026-10-31) was found. So the condition appears met. $35M after 25.5% tax over 367M shares is about $0.07, room to lift the $2.35-2.45 adjusted EPS guide about 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2026-08-27): adjusted EPS guide raised $0.05 (partly on Section 301 relief) despite a sales miss, stock +12.94%. Q3 FY25 (2025-11-20): operating-margin guide raised, +8.24%.
findings.why_not_priced: Full-year EPS consensus is $2.33, below the guide's low end of $2.35 (Earnings Whispers), and EPS estimates are down 0.7% over 60 days (Investing.com). So the Street has not added the $35M; if it had, full-year consensus would sit near $2.47-2.50. Earnings Whispers does mention the 'potential $35 million' benefit, so it is known but not modelled. Some sourcing countries are in the 12.5% tier, not 10%, so the benefit could be smaller, and Gap may reinvest it in Old Navy pricing, as it did with half the Section 122 relief.
findings.independence: Tariff rates and effective date from law-firm and Federal Register summaries: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/28/2026-15181/notice-of-actions-in-section-301-investigations-of-acts-policies-and-practices-of-various-economies and https://www.gtlaw.com/en/insights/2026/7/ustr-imposes-new-section-301-forced-labor-tariffs-on-imports-from-60-economies. Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/GAP/23177) restates the $35M.

findings.finding: Of a $417M net IEEPA tariff refund recognised in Q2 (about $512M gross, less about $95M committed to vendors), only $95M had been received in Q2 and 'the remainder [is] expected in Q3'. So about $400M+ of cash should have landed in the quarter, on top of $2.5B of cash and investments, with about $400M left on the buyback authorisation after $600M of year-to-date repurchases. That leaves room for a new or accelerated buyback announcement with the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: an accelerated repurchase and $200M of open-market buybacks came with the +12.9% print. Buybacks were not singled out as the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview found mentions a new authorisation. A larger buyback would show up as a lower share count in full-year EPS consensus ($2.33 is below the guide, so it does not). Speculative: no company statement promises one.
findings.independence: The call script, from the same company on the same day, states $400M remaining under the authorisation: https://s204.q4cdn.com/320226404/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Gap-Inc-Q2-2026-Earnings-Conference-Call-Script.pdf. Both are company documents, so this counts once.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: on 2026-11-10 UBS flagged buyer positioning as crowded (12.9 against a 2.6 historical average) and a profit-taking risk on an unchanged guide. Since then the stock fell about 12.6%, including -6.2% on 2026-11-16 with no company news, during a sector rotation from off-price and apparel into defensives. Short interest is modest at 23.8M shares and 4.87 days to cover. The crowding has probably partly cleared, so it nets to about zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into the 2026-08-27 print the stock had fallen and analysts had downgraded in early August (Jefferies, Barclays, Wells Fargo), then rose +12.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. Filed so judges can see that the crowded long UBS described has been hit since; the sign is not determinable.
findings.independence: The UBS positioning read is a different source: https://www.tradingsat.com/actualites/informations-societes/gap-flechit-a-wall-street-ubs-prevoit-des-resultats-sans-relief-1173538.html. Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/gap/shortinterest.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26 is the first call since Michael Francis took over as Old Navy brand President and CEO on 2026-11-02, succeeding Haio Barbeito. The CEO had admitted 'we didn't execute well on our seasonal assortment'. A new brand head raises the chance of a more cautious Old Navy holiday outlook, or a reset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The change was announced with Q2 on 2026-08-27, a +12.9% day. No separate reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition is known. Whether the new head resets the Old Navy plan only shows on the call. The size is near zero because the direction is unknown.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-18 CTV reported that Canada's Competition Bureau obtained a court order to advance its investigation into 'potentially false or misleading claims' by Old Navy and Gap. Gap says it is cooperating, and there is no finding of wrongdoing.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in size. Canada is a small share of sales, and any penalty would be a one-off. Filed for completeness.

baseline_tension: The mild negative lean agrees with the -16.9% 20-day run-up, which suggests the revenue worries are at least partly priced. The skew is balanced, and the tariff-driven EPS-guide upside cuts against the negatives, so p_up stays near 50 (48).
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the Q3 low-end revenue finding sits inside the company's own guided range, so it moved toward 0 (-0.8 to -0.5). The EPS bar is disputed ($0.73/$0.76/$0.78), so nothing is sized on EPS; revenue rests on two agreeing sources.
Lesson 5: Census and TJX weather is macro-to-company transmission, and TJX's consolidated beat of plan partly contradicts it, so it shrank from -0.6 to -0.4.

Lesson 3: the positioning finding's own caveat (the stock fell 12.6% after UBS flagged crowding) argues it away, so it resolved to 0.0 from -0.3. The Old Navy CEO finding's direction is unknown, so -0.2 became -0.1.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the UBS traffic finding was published 2026-11-10 and the stock fell since, so it is partly priced; it moved from -0.8 to -0.7.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (4.87 days to cover, about 7-10% of float, not crowded), so the negatives were not shrunk further for squeeze risk.
Lesson 2: the tariff relief flows into the guide, so it is filed as guidance and left unchanged at +0.8. The refund cash is filed as capital_return and left at +0.3.
Pessimism-artefact note: six of eight draft findings were negative, so p_up moved from 47 to 48 and expected_move_pct from -0.75 to -0.5.
